validity.researcher_notes: gem.wiki was 403/Cloudflare-blocked this run (wiki_citations.json empty for this scope), so I went straight to open-web research per the scope note. EXISTENCE: real, independently confirmed. The Pakistan ECC (Economic Coordination Committee) approved, on 30 May 2018, a request by Bahria Foundation (a Pakistan Navy welfare trust) for Interstate Gas Systems (ISGS, a Government Holdings/Petroleum Division subsidiary -- matches GEM's Parent field) to construct a pipeline from the proposed Bahria Foundation LNG terminal at Sonmiani (Lasbela district, Balochistan) to Nawabshah (Sindh), reported in detail by The Nation (19 Jun 2018, https://www.nation.com.pk/19-Jun-2018/govt-to-lay-310km-pipeline-to-connect-lng-terminal-with-nawabshah -- verified OK, contains '310', 'Nawabshah', '1200'). A second, independent outlet (Zameen News, 27 Mar 2019, https://www.zameen.com/news/bahria-foundation-may-establish-lng-terminal.html -- verified OK) separately corroborates the Bahria Foundation LNG terminal at Sonmiani being tied into a 'Hub-Nawabshah gas pipeline project', confirming the project's existence and route concept from a different origin, though it gives no exact length/capacity figures. Two supporting (non-cited, engineering-firm portfolio) pages -- Exponent Engineers' FEED review and PITCO's feasibility-study page for the Bahria Foundation LNG Terminal Project -- corroborate the terminal side of the project but describe only a short (~7km, 32-inch) SUBSEA line to shore, which is a DIFFERENT, shorter segment than this 310km onshore trunk to Nawabshah -- I did not use their pipe diameter for this row to avoid conflating the two segments. CLASSIFICATION: correct. The Nation article describes a full transmission-grade system (metering station, main-line block valve stations, receiving stations, cathodic protection, SCADA, river/canal/railway crossings, 40-year design life) crossing multiple provinces -- a transmission trunk, not a gathering/feeder line; Fuel=Gas is correct (it carries regasified LNG as pipeline-quality natural gas). DUPLICATE: checked against the 6-row Pakistan-gas roster. Not a duplicate of P0452 (Iran-Pakistan, different corridor/endpoints), P0766 (TAPI, ends in Punjab), P3101 (Pakistan Stream, Karachi-based), P3174 (Off-Shore Gas Pipeline, len=1500/cap=1000 -- close in concept, since ISGS's own site lists a distinct 'OSGP' project, but the numbers and stated route don't match this row and I found no source tying them together -- flagging as worth a second look but not calling it a duplicate on current evidence), or P3178 (Sawan-Lahore, different origin field). Also confirmed this is NOT the separate, much larger 'Gwadar-Nawabshah' LNG/pipeline project (Rs203bn/US$2bn, ISGS-CNPC, ~700km) that recurs heavily in search results under a similar name -- that is a different corridor (Gwadar, not Sonmiani/Hub) and is not in the current roster. ATTRIBUTION: Owner1=Interstate Gas Systems 100% confirmed by the Nation article ('ISGS would construct and operate the pipeline'); StartLocation/Province (Sonmiani/Balochistan) and EndLocation/Province (Nawabshah/Sindh) confirmed by both sources. Minor caveat: the Nation article's actual route detail says the pipe runs 'Hub to Dureji (158km)' then 'Dureji to Nawabshah (152km)' -- Hub is the nearby town/district seat serving Sonmiani Bay, not a literal renaming, so I don't read this as an endpoint error, just a precision note for whoever routes this in the geometry tool. SPEC: LengthKnown=310km and Capacity=1200 MMcf/d both match the Nation article's '310 km' and 'capable of transporting 700 to 1200 MMCFD' (GEM recorded the range's ceiling, a defensible choice). Because only one outlet gives the exact numbers, I'm scoring the length/capacity/owner fills tier=medium (single strong, government-approval-sourced article) even though existence itself is tier=high (2 independent outlets). Diameter is correctly left blank -- no source gives a diameter for the 310km trunk specifically (only for the unrelated 7km subsea segment).

fills.researcher_notes: Pipeline carries re-gasified LNG (natural gas) per the source; single-source ref for this field.
Source describes a 310km high-pressure trunk with metering/block-valve/receiving stations, SCADA and CP -- transmission-grade infrastructure, not a gathering/feeder line.
ECC approved the ISGS construction request on 30 May 2018 per the article; matches recorded ProposalYear=2018 exactly.

Source gives a design range of '700 to 1200 MMCFD'; GEM records the ceiling (1200), a defensible reading of design capacity. Only one outlet gives an exact figure, so scored medium despite the source's authority (it reports an ECC-approved government summary).

Exact 310km match, broken down in the source as Hub-Dureji (158km) + Dureji-Nawabshah (152km). Only one outlet gives the exact figure (Zameen corroborates the project/route concept but no number), so scored medium.

Both sources confirm the Sonmiani (Balochistan) to Nawabshah (Sindh) route/tie-in; two independent outlets, so scored high. Note: the Nation article's route breakdown starts from 'Hub' (the district town adjoining Sonmiani Bay) rather than literally 'Sonmiani' -- a precision nuance for anyone mapping exact endpoint coordinates, not an error in the recorded value.

Nation article: 'ISGS would construct and operate the pipeline, while Bahria Foundation would act as the lead organisation responsible for LNG purchase/sale arrangements' -- matches recorded Owner1=Interstate Gas Systems 100%, and matches GEM's Parent field (Government Holdings Pvt Ltd, ISGS's parent). Single-source, so scored medium; could not independently verify the 100% ownership share (no ISGS site access -- isgs.com.pk returned 403 to both WebFetch and curl, and its own Wayback captures for the specific project galleries only archived the site's homepage shell, not the gallery content).

No source calls this pipeline 'shelved' specifically -- it went from ECC-approved (2018) straight to FEED-completed/under-development narrative (2018-2019) with no news since. Not filling a ref for the current 'shelved' value; see the status_reviews entry below proposing a status change to 'cancelled' under the staleness rule instead.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Timeline found: PITCO feasibility study for the Bahria Foundation LNG Terminal Project (Jul 2015-Mar 2017); ECC approval of the ISGS pipeline construction request (30 May 2018), reported by The Nation (19 Jun 2018); Exponent Engineers FEED review dated May 2018; Zameen News still describing the terminal as at the ECC-consideration stage in Mar 2019 (the most recent dated, independently-verifiable evidence I could find). I searched extensively (English and Urdu) for any 2020-2026 news on the Bahria Foundation Sonmiani LNG terminal or its Sonmiani-Nawabshah/Hub-Nawabshah pipeline -- found nothing: no completion, construction-start, cancellation, or revival story, and no mention in any of the Gwadar-Nawabshah-project revival coverage (that is a separate, unrelated project). ISGS's own site (isgs.com.pk) is Cloudflare-blocked to both WebFetch and curl; its Wayback Machine captures for the relevant project-gallery pages only preserved the site's homepage shell, not gallery content, so I could not check ISGS's own current project list. Engineering-firm portfolio pages (Exponent, PITCO) describing 'FEED completed'/'under development' are undated relative to today and read as legacy 2018-era project descriptions, not current updates. Given the current recorded Status is already 'shelved' and there is no independent evidence of any activity in roughly 7 years (since the 2019 evidence), this satisfies the 'shelved >=4y -> cancelled' dormancy rule. Presumed inference only -- no fabricated ref, per standing rule 2.

summary: P3173 (Somiani-Nawabshah Gas Pipeline) is a real, correctly classified ISGS transmission trunk tied to the (also dormant) Bahria Foundation Sonmiani LNG terminal -- confirmed by 2 independent outlets (Nation 2018 government-approval report, Zameen 2019) with recorded length/capacity/owner/route matching the Nation article exactly; not a duplicate of any other roster row. 8 refs staged (7 REFS_ADDED, Status left UNRESOLVED); status flagged stale -> proposed change to cancelled (dormant since ~2019, exceeding the shelved->cancelled 4-year threshold), Presumed, no fabricated ref.
